agree.reason: The salon-only focus and the free-month guarantee will appeal to her, but she compares $199 a month with the $600 a year her cousin charges, and nothing on the page tells her she can keep her cousin for her taxes or leave at any time, so she will probably not book.

honest.reason: Saying 'Every month's books are closed by the 10th' as plain fact goes beyond the record, because she missed that date 3 times last year and the guarantee only started in January, and 'books your accountant won't have to fix' promises more than the 9 client reports can support.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw numbers are repeated but never worked into anything: 29 of 31 salons kept, with no client leaving except through a sale, isn't stated as a retention rate, and $199 a month isn't set against what payroll and accountant savings would otherwise cost.

right_comparison.reason: The page never describes her actual alternative, a once-a-year catch-up by a relative for $600 with no monthly books and no payroll, so she can't see what she would gain by switching.

qualification.reason: The guarantee gives a date and a consequence she can check (books closed by the 10th or that month is free), but the $800 hedge is a vague disclaimer and gives her nothing to verify.

objections.reason: Her two real objections, the cost compared with her cousin and her loyalty to him, go unanswered even though the brief's facts would answer them: she doesn't do income tax so the cousin can keep doing her return, there's no contract and 30 days' notice ends it, and Carla managed a salon herself.

fit.reason: It is close to 350 words, is set out as clear sections in sales-page form and ends with the booking button as asked.
